title: The EU AI Act's 2 August 2026 high-risk deadline did not land: the Digital Omnibus moved it to December 2027, six days before it would have applied
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, was published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July — three days after publication, an urgency the recitals attribute to the imminent general application of the AI Act on 2 August 2026. It amends Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and pushes full high-risk obligations for standalone Annex III systems from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and for Annex I systems embedded in products already covered by EU product-safety law to 2 August 2028. Two earlier signals in this corpus (2026-03-23-05 and 2026-06-29-15) were written on the assumption that the August date would hold; the high-risk half of that expectation is now wrong. What did not move is Article 50: transparency obligations still applied from 2 August 2026, so providers of chatbots and generative systems must still disclose that a user is interacting with AI, synthetic audio, image, video and text must still be marked as artificially generated, and deepfake disclosure still applies. For software organisations the practical position is a split calendar — the disclosure and labelling work that touches product surfaces is live now; the conformity-assessment, technical-documentation, risk-management and CE-marking programme for Annex III systems has sixteen more months.
source: EUR-Lex (Official Journal of the European Union)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
whyItMatters: Teams that sequenced their compliance work around 2 August 2026 now have a different critical path. The expensive Annex III programme has slack; the cheap-sounding Article 50 labelling work is already overdue if it was deprioritised behind it.
This corrects two signals already published here. Anyone who read the earlier items and planned from them should re-check what they committed to and when.

A deadline moved by emergency legislation six days before it applied is itself information about the regime: the schedule is negotiable under industry pressure, which argues for building compliance capability rather than date-driven projects.

Deferral is not repeal. December 2027 for Annex III means the risk-management system, data governance, documentation and human-oversight requirements still have to exist, and organisations that stand down entirely will rebuild the same programme under worse time pressure.
recommendedActions: Verify that Article 50 disclosure and synthetic-content marking are actually shipped in EU-facing products, since these obligations applied from 2 August 2026 regardless of the deferral.

Re-baseline the Annex III compliance plan to 2 December 2027 rather than cancelling it, and keep the classification work — knowing which of your systems are high-risk is the input to everything else and does not expire.

Check whether any internal AI use touches Annex III employment use cases such as worker evaluation or task allocation; AI-assisted coding tools generally do not, but AI applied to developer performance management can.

Have counsel confirm the position for your specific systems before standing anything down. This item summarises the regulation; it is not legal advice and the amendments also touch aviation and machinery regulations.
risksAndCaveats: The regulation number, publication and entry-into-force dates and the new deadlines are confirmed against EUR-Lex. The detail that Article 50 transparency obligations were unaffected and applied from 2 August 2026 is taken from secondary legal commentary, which was consistent across sources but was not verified against the consolidated text in this run.
Attempts to retrieve two law-firm analyses (Gibson Dunn, Latham & Watkins) were blocked during this run, so the reading here rests on the Official Journal citation plus non-law-firm commentary.

National implementation, enforcement bodies and penalty practice vary by member state and are not covered by the deferral; the changed date says nothing about how strictly the obligations that do apply will be enforced.
